options: Three lines, each with the count 1
An error, because the input is not sorted
questions.why: `uniq` only joins lines that are next to each other. The two `b` lines are separated by `a`, so each line is its own group.

wrong.0: That would need `uniq` to sort first. It does not.
wrong.1: That is the answer after `sort`. `uniq` neither sorts nor joins lines that are apart.
wrong.3: `uniq` accepts unsorted input without complaint. It only gives a useless answer.

questions.prompt: A script is run as `./r.sh term 1.log`. What is `$#` inside it?
questions.why: Without quotes the shell splits on the space, so the script gets two arguments: `term` and `1.log`.

wrong.0: The shell does not know you meant one name. Only quotes keep it together.
wrong.2: `$#` does not count the script's own name.
wrong.3: `$#` is the number of arguments. You are thinking of `$?`, the exit code.

questions.prompt: A check script in CI contains `if [ ! -r $1 ]; then echo "cannot read"; exit 0; fi`. What is most wrong?
options: It exits 0, so the caller thinks it worked
questions.why: Exit code 0 means success. CI would go green although the file could not be read.

wrong.1: `-r` is a real test: "the file exists and I can read it".
wrong.2: Any command can be used inside `if`.

questions.prompt: Where should the line `usage: report.sh FILE` go?
options: Nowhere; the exit code is enough
questions.why: Standard error is for messages to people. A pipeline that reads the output never mistakes it for data.

wrong.0: The next command in a pipe would read the usage line as data.
wrong.1: The person running the script would never see it.
wrong.2: The exit code tells a program; the person still needs to know what to type.

questions.prompt: What does `sort -k1,1nr` print for the lines `9 x`, `10 y`, `2 z`?
questions.why: `n` compares the first column as a number and `r` puts the biggest first: 10, 9, 2.

wrong.0: That is text order reversed, as if `n` were missing.
wrong.2: That is number order, smallest first, as if `r` were missing.
wrong.3: That is text order: `10` comes before `2` because `1` comes before `2`.

questions.prompt: What does `set -e` change in a script?
options: It prints every command before running it
It makes a variable that was never set an error
The script stops at the first command that fails
questions.why: With `-e`, a failing command ends the script instead of letting it carry on with bad data.

questions.prompt: GPIS: why must a check script in `scripts/` exit with a non-zero code when it finds a problem?
options: So that the message is printed in red
Because Git refuses to commit scripts that exit 0
It does not matter, as long as the message is clear
CI reads only the exit code, and 0 means "all good"
questions.why: CI does not read the text. A problem that exits 0 makes the run green, and the problem ships.

wrong.0: Colour is not the signal. Many CI screens show no colour at all.
wrong.1: Git has no such rule. It stores scripts; it does not run them.
wrong.2: Nobody reads the messages of a green run.
